assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
scope is composing a single scene from a given 2-3 entity bundle; entity linking/disambiguation and asset rendering are delegated to sibling KBs
a target audience segment with an inspectable shared schema is available
final legal/compliance adjudication of hard sensitivity calls is owned by a compliance function, not the writer
exclusions: entity disambiguation and relatedness scoring internals (delegated to link__entity_relevance)
audience segment discovery and modeling internals (delegated to niche__audience_segmentation)
visual asset rendering, typesetting, and production tooling
paid distribution, ad-buying, and post-publish analytics attribution
source_description: heuristic prior estimates for multi-entity comedic/narrative scene composition work units, informed by incongruity-resolution and benign-violation humor theory, classical dramatic structure, meme studies, and virality research; no supplied dataset
source_citation: Suls 1972 (incongruity-resolution two-stage model, in Goldstein & McGhee eds., The Psychology of Humor); McGraw & Warren 2010 Benign Violation Theory (Psychological Science 21:1141-1149); Freytag 1863 Die Technik des Dramas (Freytag's pyramid); Dawkins 1976 The Selfish Gene ch.11 (meme); Shifman 2014 Memes in Digital Culture (MIT Press); Berger & Milkman 2012 What Makes Online Content Viral? (Journal of Marketing Research 49:192-205)

competency_questions.question: How are the 2-3 entities selected, verified related, and given a single contrast axis?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ENTITY_BUNDLE selects 2-3 related entities; ENTITY_CONTRAST_AXIS fixes one contrast axis

competency_questions.question: How is the target audience segment and its reference schema and register defined?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AUDIENCE_FIT fixes the segment schema; TONE_REGISTER sets a matching register

competency_questions.question: How is the humor engineered as a resolvable incongruity over the entities' contrast?
How is the violation kept benign and aligned with the chosen register?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BENIGN_VIOLATION sets violation intensity; SENSITIVITY_AWARENESS and TONE_REGISTER keep it benign

competency_questions.question: How is the comedic micro-structure (setup/turn/punchline, rule of three) arranged and verified readable?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMEDIC_STRUCTURE orders the beats; CLARITY_READABILITY verifies first-contact comprehension

competency_questions.question: How is a proven meme format chosen and the entities mapped into its slots?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MEME_FORMAT_REUSE selects a live format and maps entities to slots; SCENE_ASSEMBLY integrates it

competency_questions.question: How is a micro-narrative arc shaped over the scene?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NARRATIVE_BEATS imposes exposition/rising/climax/button on the scene

competency_questions.question: How are cultural references chosen and the relatability-vs-niche tradeoff set?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CULTURAL_REFERENCE selects segment references; RELATABILITY_VS_NICHE sets the reach-vs-depth point

competency_questions.question: How is the reach ceiling versus per-viewer intensity tradeoff decided?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RELATABILITY_VS_NICHE sets the target point on the reach-vs-depth curve

competency_questions.question: How is harmful framing avoided and which calls are escalated to compliance?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SENSITIVITY_AWARENESS screens harm targets and escalates; SENSITIVITY_GATE is the final hard stop

competency_questions.question: How is the scene optimized for the empirical share drivers (emotion, identity, surprise)?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SHAREABILITY_DRIVERS audits arousal/identity/surprise levers; SHAREABILITY_FORECAST counts them pre-publish

competency_questions.question: How is timing/current-event relevance decided and gated for sensitivity?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TIMING_RELEVANCE sizes the window and gates topical ties; SENSITIVITY_GATE re-verifies them

competency_questions.question: How is the assembled scene scored for clarity, humor, and spread before publish?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CLARITY_READABILITY, HUMOR_QUALITY_SCORE and SHAREABILITY_FORECAST gate the assembled scene

competency_questions.question: How is the publish-ready scene packaged so its creative and safety choices are auditable?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SCENE_HANDOFF packages the artifact, choices, sign-off, timing and forecast rationale

glossary.definition: the two-stage humor process where a setup creates an expectation, an incongruity violates it, and a punchline supplies a rule that resolves the surprise (Suls 1972)
the condition under which something is funny: it is a violation yet simultaneously benign/safe (McGraw & Warren 2010)
a comedic pattern where two beats establish an expectation and a third subverts it
a recognizable template with conventional form, content slots, and stance, propagated by imitation (Shifman 2014)
the dramatic arc of exposition, rising action, climax, falling action, denouement (Freytag 1863)
the single shared-frame dimension (status, scale, era, values) the entities are played against
the in-group knowledge, experiences, and platform norms the target segment already holds
an attribute that raises sharing likelihood: high-arousal emotion, identity expression, or surprise (Berger & Milkman 2012)
directing a violation at a less-powerful or vulnerable target, a harmful (non-benign) framing to avoid
the short period during which a current event or trend carries borrowable attention

nodes.definition: Select the 2-3 entities the scene will compose and verify they are genuinely related (shared domain, rivalry, category, or a known relationship) rather than arbitrary. The bundle is the scene's raw material: a pair anchors a single contrast, a triad adds a third beat (rule-of-three) without diluting focus. Reject bundles of 1 (no relation to play) or >=4 (cognitive overload, no clear contrast).

base.update_signal: entity-relatedness threshold or max-arity policy changes

pros.claim: A vetted 2-3 entity bundle gives the scene exactly one contrast to exploit, the documented sweet spot for a single readable joke or beat
pros.example: pairing a budget airline with a luxury one sets up one clean status contrast

cons.claim: Forcing a relationship onto unrelated entities yields a non-sequitur the audience cannot resolve
cons.example: jamming a tax form and a dolphin together with no shared frame reads as noise

failure_modes: arity exceeds 3 and the scene loses focus
entities share no frame so no contrast exists
acceptance_tests: bundle has 2 or 3 entities with an explicit shared frame and a named relationship

nodes.definition: Define the target audience segment and the reference frame the scene must speak in: the in-group knowledge, shared experiences, and platform norms the segment already holds. A scene lands only when its references resolve inside the audience's existing schema; a reference outside it reads as confusing or excluding. This node fixes the schema every later choice (format, references, register) is tuned against.

base.update_signal: target segment redefinition or platform-norm shift

pros.claim: Calibrating to a concrete segment schema turns 'is this funny?' into 'is this funny to them?', a far more answerable question
pros.example: a scene for backend engineers can assume what a flaky CI pipeline feels like

cons.claim: Over-fitting to one narrow segment can shrink reach below a viable threshold
cons.example: an inside joke only 200 people understand caps the ceiling

failure_modes: scene tuned to a schema the audience does not actually hold
platform register mismatched to segment
acceptance_tests: target segment named with an explicit shared-schema inventory the scene will use
revisit_triggers: a reference-miss (audience didn't get it) is reported

nodes.definition: Engineer the humor as Suls' (1972) two-stage process: a setup creates an expectation, an incongruity violates it, and a punchline supplies a cognitive rule that resolves the surprise (the 'aha'). Humor lives in the gap being both surprising AND retrospectively makeable-sense-of; pure surprise without a resolving rule reads as random, and a fully expected turn reads as flat. For a 2-3 entity scene the incongruity is the unexpected relation drawn between the entities.

base.update_signal: humor model revised or resolution-rule criteria change

pros.claim: A resolvable incongruity is the empirically recurring core of verbal humor: the audience does the closing work and rewards it with a laugh
pros.example: two CEOs feuding resolved by both using the same generic stock photo

cons.claim: If the resolving rule is too obscure the incongruity never resolves and the joke dies as confusion
cons.example: a punchline needing three layers of niche lore most readers lack

failure_modes: surprise with no resolving rule (random)
no surprise at all (predictable, flat)
acceptance_tests: scene exhibits a clear setup, an incongruity, and a resolution the target audience can close
revisit_triggers: audience reports confusion rather than amusement

nodes.definition: Apply McGraw & Warren's (2010) Benign Violation Theory: humor arises when something is simultaneously a violation (of a norm, expectation, or dignity) AND benign (safe, playful, distant). Tune the scene into the band where the violation is felt but stays benign. Too benign = not funny (no violation); too severe / too close = offensive or distressing (not benign). This node sets the violation intensity that INCONGRUITY_RESOLUTION's turn carries.

base.update_signal: benign-violation calibration or norm context changes

pros.claim: The two dials (violation present, violation benign) explain both why something is funny and why it crosses a line, in one model
pros.example: a gentle roast of a beloved brand stays benign; the same words at a tragedy do not

cons.claim: Benignity is audience- and context-relative, so a violation benign to one segment is harmful to another
cons.example: an in-group joke that reads as cruel to outsiders who see the clip out of context

failure_modes: violation absent so the scene is inert
violation severe/too-close so it harms rather than amuses
acceptance_tests: the scene's violation is detectable yet judged benign by the target segment in its likely contexts
revisit_triggers: a benign-to-harmful boundary case is reported

nodes.definition: Impose comedic micro-structure on the scene: a setup that establishes the pattern, a turn that breaks it, and a punchline that lands the break; for triads use the rule of three (two beats establish a pattern, the third subverts it). Order and economy matter: the funniest word/image goes last, and every element not serving the turn is cut. This is the surface arrangement that delivers INCONGRUITY_RESOLUTION's gap.

base.update_signal: comedic-structure conventions or platform format constraints change

pros.claim: Putting the payload word/image last and cutting everything inessential maximizes the surprise impact of a fixed gap
pros.example: two normal panels then a third that violates the pattern lands harder than a front-loaded reveal

cons.claim: Rigid three-beat structure can feel formulaic when the audience has seen the template too often
cons.example: yet-another 'expectation / expectation / subversion' grid that reads as template fatigue

failure_modes: punchline not in terminal position so impact leaks
padding dilutes the turn
acceptance_tests: scene has an identifiable setup, turn, and terminal punchline with no inessential elements

nodes.definition: Select a proven meme format (a recognizable template with conventional form, content slots, and stance) as the scaffold the scene is poured into. Per Shifman (2014), a meme is a group of items sharing form/content/stance propagated by imitation; reusing a live format gives the audience an instant frame and signals in-group fluency, lowering the comprehension cost of the joke. The format's known slots constrain where each entity and the turn go.

base.update_signal: format popularity decay or a new dominant template emerges

pros.claim: A live, recognized format is a comprehension shortcut: the audience already knows how to read it, so the scene spends its budget on the turn not the frame
pros.example: the 'two buttons' sweating-choice format instantly frames a dilemma between two entities

cons.claim: Formats decay; a stale or overused template signals lateness and lowers shareability
cons.example: using a meme format six months past its peak reads as out-of-touch

failure_modes: chosen format is dead/overused
entities forced into slots the format does not support
acceptance_tests: format is currently live for the segment and its slots map cleanly to the entities and the turn

nodes.definition: Shape the scene as a compressed micro-story using Freytag's (1863) dramatic structure scaled to a single unit: exposition (who/what), rising tension (the entities collide), climax (the turn), and a brief denouement/button. Even a one-panel or single-line scene benefits from an implied arc; beats give the audience a tiny story to inhabit, which raises engagement beyond a static juxtaposition. Beats carry the incongruity through time rather than presenting it flat.

base.update_signal: narrative-beat schema or platform length norms change

pros.claim: A micro-arc gives even a single image a beginning-middle-end the viewer completes, raising dwell and recall over a flat juxtaposition
pros.example: a three-panel build where tension rises before the climactic turn outperforms a single static contrast

cons.claim: Forcing a full arc into a tight format can bloat the scene past the platform's attention window
cons.example: a five-beat story stuffed into a format meant for a single punch reads as slow

failure_modes: arc bloats past the attention window
beats present the contrast flat with no rise
acceptance_tests: scene has at least an implied exposition, climax (turn), and button within the format's length

nodes.definition: Layer in cultural and local references (in-jokes, regional touchstones, subculture lore) that the target segment recognizes, raising resonance and the feeling that the scene was made for them. A landed reference is a strong identity and shareability signal; a missed reference is dead weight or, worse, an exclusion cue. References must be checked against AUDIENCE_FIT's schema, not the author's own.

base.update_signal: the referenced cultural touchstone ages out or shifts meaning

pros.claim: A reference the segment owns acts as an identity handshake: getting it is itself part of the reward and a reason to share
pros.example: a niche reference to a specific in-community catchphrase signals 'this creator is one of us'

cons.claim: References are perishable and segment-bound; one that ages out or excludes outsiders caps reach and can read as gatekeeping
cons.example: a reference to last year's drama that newer audience members never saw

failure_modes: reference recognized by too few to matter
reference reads as exclusionary to adjacent audience
acceptance_tests: each reference has an estimated recognition rate above threshold for the target segment

nodes.definition: Manage the core tradeoff between broad relatability (a universal experience many recognize) and insider/niche appeal (deep resonance for few). Broad scenes maximize reach but risk blandness; niche scenes maximize intensity and shareability-per-viewer but cap the ceiling. This node sets the target point on that curve given the segment and goal, and decides how many references are insider vs universal.

base.update_signal: growth goal shifts between reach and depth, moving the target point

pros.claim: Naming the target point explicitly prevents accidental drift to bland-broad or impenetrable-niche and aligns the scene with the goal
pros.example: a growth-phase scene leans relatable; a loyalty-phase scene leans insider

cons.claim: The optimum is unstable: the same scene can be too niche for reach goals and too broad for community goals
cons.example: a mid-niche scene satisfies neither a viral push nor a core-fan reward

failure_modes: scene drifts to bland universality with no edge
scene so niche the reach ceiling is unviable
acceptance_tests: scene's insider/universal mix matches the stated reach-vs-depth goal for this segment
revisit_triggers: reach ceiling proves too low for the goal

nodes.definition: Screen the scene for harm: avoid framing built on tragedy, ethnic/religious denigration, protected-class mockery, or punching-down at the vulnerable, and route any hard call to compliance rather than deciding it in the writing seat. This is the benign-side guardrail on BENIGN_VIOLATION: it does not kill edge, it relocates the violation off harmful targets and escalates ambiguous cases instead of guessing.

base.update_signal: platform policy, legal guidance, or protected-class scope changes

pros.claim: Relocating the violation off protected/tragic targets preserves the joke's edge while removing the harm, and escalation prevents a single writer absorbing a legal/ethical call
pros.example: redirect a roast from a person's ethnicity to their public product decision keeps it benign

cons.claim: Over-cautious screening can sand off all edge and produce inert, forgettable content
cons.example: removing every conceivable violation leaves a scene with no turn and no humor

failure_modes: harmful framing ships undetected
ambiguous case decided in the writing seat instead of escalated
acceptance_tests: scene has no tragedy/ethnic/religious/punching-down framing and all hard calls are escalated to compliance
revisit_triggers: platform policy or legal guidance changes
a harm complaint or near-miss is reported

nodes.definition: Maximize the levers that make people share, per Berger & Milkman (2012): high-arousal emotion (awe, amusement, anger, anxiety) drives sharing more than low-arousal states, and content that lets the sharer express identity or signal in-group membership travels further. Surprise (the resolved incongruity) is itself a high-arousal trigger. This node audits the scene for at least one strong share lever and strengthens the weakest.

base.update_signal: platform sharing mechanics or measured share-driver weights change

pros.claim: Auditing against named, evidence-backed share drivers (arousal, identity, surprise) turns 'will it spread?' into a checklist the scene can be strengthened against
pros.example: amusement plus an identity-signaling in-joke gives two reinforcing share reasons

cons.claim: Optimizing purely for shareability can push toward outrage-bait that wins shares but damages brand trust
cons.example: an anger-driven scene spreads but attaches the brand to a fight

failure_modes: scene has no strong share lever (low arousal, no identity hook)
share lever is outrage that harms trust
acceptance_tests: scene exhibits at least one strong, non-harmful share lever from emotion/identity/surprise
revisit_triggers: a high-quality scene underperforms on shares

nodes.definition: Decide whether and how to tie the scene to a current event, trend, or moment to ride its attention window. Timely scenes borrow the event's existing attention and feel alive, but the window is short and tying to a sensitive event (tragedy, controversy) multiplies sensitivity risk. This node sizes the window, sets a freshness deadline, and gates topical ties through SENSITIVITY_AWARENESS.

base.update_signal: the riding event's window closes or its valence shifts

pros.claim: Riding a live window borrows attention the scene would otherwise have to earn cold, sharply raising reach for time-bound effort
pros.example: a scene tied to a same-day product launch rides the launch's search and feed spike

cons.claim: Topicality is perishable and risky: a missed window wastes the work and a tie to a sensitive event can blow up
cons.example: publishing a 'trend' joke a day late, or tying levity to an unfolding tragedy

failure_modes: window closes before publish
topical tie attaches the scene to a sensitive event
acceptance_tests: any topical tie has a sized window, a freshness deadline, and passed the sensitivity gate
revisit_triggers: a topical tie's valence shifts negative

nodes.definition: Choose the single contrast axis the entities will be played against (status, scale, competence, era, values, expectation) so the relation drawn between them is sharp and one-dimensional. A clear axis is what makes the incongruity legible; multiple competing axes muddy the turn. For a triad the axis must order all three (two conform, one breaks).

base.update_signal: contrast-axis taxonomy or entity attributes change

pros.claim: One sharp axis makes the incongruity instantly legible and gives the punchline a clean fulcrum
pros.example: playing two phones purely on price makes the status flip read in a glance

cons.claim: A single axis can flatten genuinely multidimensional entities into a reductive comparison
cons.example: reducing two rich brands to one price point may miss the funnier values contrast

failure_modes: multiple competing axes muddy the turn
axis fails to order a triad's third entity
acceptance_tests: exactly one contrast axis is chosen and it orders all 2-3 entities legibly
revisit_triggers: audience misreads which axis is in play

nodes.definition: Set the tone and register (deadpan, absurd, wholesome, sarcastic, earnest) to match both the audience schema and the platform's norms, and hold it consistently across the scene. Register is the carrier wave for the joke: a turn that is funny in a deadpan register can fall flat or read as mean in a sarcastic one. Register must agree with BENIGN_VIOLATION (a harsh register can tip a benign violation into a harmful one).

base.update_signal: platform register norms or brand voice guidelines change

pros.claim: A register matched to segment and platform makes the same joke land warm instead of cold and keeps a violation benign
pros.example: a wholesome-deadpan register keeps a roast affectionate rather than cruel

cons.claim: Register and content can fight: an edgy turn in an earnest register reads as tonally confused
cons.example: a sarcastic punchline inside a sincere brand voice jars

failure_modes: register tips a benign violation into harm
register drifts mid-scene
acceptance_tests: one register is chosen, fits segment and platform, and is held consistently across the scene

nodes.definition: Compose the vetted entities, chosen format, contrast axis, beats, and register into one coherent scene draft: place each entity in its format slot, route the contrast through the comedic structure and narrative beats, and ensure the parts cohere into a single readable unit rather than a collage. This is the integration step where format slots, beats, and the turn are reconciled into one artifact.

base.update_signal: assembly contract between format/beats/structure changes

pros.claim: A single integration step forces the format, beats, axis, and register to agree before any polish, catching incoherent collages early
pros.example: the contrast axis, the format's slots, and the punchline position all line up in one draft

cons.claim: Premature assembly before the format or axis is settled produces churn as the draft is rebuilt repeatedly
cons.example: assembling around a format that later proves dead wastes the layout work

failure_modes: parts read as a collage not a unit
format slots and beats contradict each other
acceptance_tests: a single coherent scene draft exists with every entity placed and beats/format/axis reconciled
revisit_triggers: a draft reads as incoherent in review

nodes.definition: Verify the scene is comprehended on first contact within the platform's scroll-speed window: the entities are identifiable, the contrast axis is obvious, and the turn resolves without external explanation. A joke that needs a caption explaining it has failed comprehension. This gate measures whether the incongruity actually resolves for a fresh viewer, not just for the author.

base.update_signal: platform scroll-speed norms or comprehension threshold changes

pros.claim: A fresh-viewer comprehension gate catches author's-curse failures where the scene is clear only to the person who built it
pros.example: a test reader who gets the turn in two seconds without explanation passes the gate

cons.claim: Optimizing purely for instant clarity can strip the rewarding layer that makes a scene re-shareable
cons.example: over-explaining the contrast removes the satisfying 'figure it out' beat

failure_modes: scene needs an explanatory caption to land
entities unidentifiable at scroll speed
acceptance_tests: a fresh target-segment viewer comprehends entities and turn within the scroll window with no caption

nodes.definition: Score the assembled scene's humor quality: does the incongruity actually resolve (Suls), does the violation read as benign (McGraw & Warren), is the punchline in terminal position, and does a target-segment sample find it amusing rather than confusing or flat. Produces a go/no-go and a weakest-link diagnosis routed back to the humor or assembly nodes for one revision pass.

base.update_signal: humor scoring rubric or sample-panel composition changes

pros.claim: A rubric tied to the two humor theories plus a sample panel converts a subjective laugh into a repeatable, diagnosable score
pros.example: a scene that confuses 6 of 10 testers fails resolution and is sent back to the incongruity node

cons.claim: Small or unrepresentative sample panels give noisy scores that can reject good scenes or pass weak ones
cons.example: a panel of 3 colleagues over-rates an in-house in-joke

failure_modes: weak scene passes on a biased panel
good scene rejected on a noisy small sample
acceptance_tests: scene's incongruity resolves, violation is benign, and a representative sample finds it amusing

nodes.definition: Run the final pre-publish harm gate on the fully assembled scene: re-screen the integrated artifact (not just the raw idea) for harmful framing, verify any topical tie is still benign, and require an explicit compliance sign-off for any escalated item before publish. This gate is the hard stop; a scene that is funny but fails here does not ship.

base.update_signal: compliance policy, legal guidance, or escalation protocol changes

pros.claim: Screening the final integrated artifact catches harms that only emerge from the combination of parts, and a hard sign-off prevents a funny-but-harmful scene shipping on momentum
pros.example: two individually fine elements that combine into a slur are caught only at the assembled stage

cons.claim: A hard gate at the end can cause expensive late rework if sensitivity was ignored upstream
cons.example: a fully produced scene killed at the gate wastes all the assembly effort

failure_modes: harm emergent from combination ships
escalated item published without sign-off
acceptance_tests: assembled scene re-screened clean, topical tie re-verified benign, and all escalations signed off before publish

nodes.definition: Forecast the scene's likely spread before publish by auditing it against the share drivers and timing window: count the strong, non-harmful share levers present, estimate the segment recognition rate of its references, and confirm the timing window is still open. Produces a spread estimate and a final strengthen-or-ship decision; it does not override the sensitivity gate.

base.update_signal: share-driver weights or platform distribution mechanics change

pros.claim: A pre-publish forecast against named drivers lets a weak-but-fixable scene be strengthened rather than published flat or scrapped
pros.example: a scene with high amusement but no identity hook is sent back to add one before publishing

cons.claim: Forecasts from heuristic drivers are uncertain and can over-promise reach, inviting disappointment or over-investment
cons.example: a scene that checks every share box still flops because the timing closed

failure_modes: forecast over-promises and the scene flops
forecast used to override the sensitivity gate
acceptance_tests: scene has counted share levers, an estimated recognition rate, and a confirmed-open window before the ship decision
revisit_triggers: forecasts diverge sharply from realized spread

nodes.definition: Package the gated scene for publish: the final scene artifact, the entity bundle and contrast axis used, the format and register, the sensitivity sign-off record, the timing window/deadline, and the forecast rationale. The handoff makes the scene reproducible, auditable, and schedulable, and records why each major creative and safety choice was made.

base.update_signal: handoff package schema or publishing-system contract changes

pros.claim: A complete handoff package makes the scene reproducible and auditable: every safety and creative call is traceable after the fact
pros.example: a reviewer can reconstruct why a topical tie was approved from the sign-off record

cons.claim: Over-heavy handoff documentation can slow time-sensitive scenes past their window
cons.example: a same-day trend scene delayed by paperwork misses the spike

failure_modes: scene ships without a sign-off record
package omits the timing deadline
acceptance_tests: handoff package contains the artifact, choices, sensitivity sign-off, timing window, and forecast rationale
revisit_triggers: a published scene cannot be audited from its package

edges.why_related: the chosen contrast axis is the dimension along which the incongruity is drawn
a failed humor score routes a revision back to the comedic structure
a comprehension failure can send the scene back to pick a clearer format
the reach-vs-depth point constrains which share levers (broad vs identity) to lean on
a harsh register can tip a benign violation toward harm, constraining the safe register set
narrative beats and comedic beats are coordinated arrangements of the same scene over time
the spread forecast must never override the sensitivity hard stop

edges.resolution_rule: keep the violation that creates the humor but relocate it off protected/tragic/vulnerable targets; escalate ambiguous cases to compliance rather than removing all edge
edges.why_related: the edge that makes a violation funny conflicts with the safety requirement that it stay benign and harm-free
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule

edges.resolution_rule: set the reach-vs-depth point from the stated goal first; then choose share levers that fit it (broad-emotion for reach, identity-signal for niche) instead of maximizing reach and depth at once
edges.why_related: broad relatability maximizes reach while insider niche maximizes per-viewer share intensity, pulling the scene in opposite directions
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule

edges.resolution_rule: let the freshness deadline create urgency but never bypass the sensitivity gate; an unsafe topical tie is dropped even if the window is closing
edges.why_related: the pressure to publish inside a short topical window conflicts with the time the sensitivity gate needs to clear a topical tie
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule

edges.resolution_rule: keep references whose estimated segment recognition clears threshold; demote or gloss references that fail the fresh-viewer comprehension gate
edges.why_related: dense insider references raise resonance but can break first-contact comprehension for the broader target viewer
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule

conflict_axes.name: benign_violation_edge_vs_harm_safety
conflict_axes.description: The violation that creates humor must stay benign; pushing edge raises laughs but risks crossing into harm, while sanding all edge kills the joke.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: relocate the violation off harmful targets; escalate ambiguous calls to compliance

conflict_axes.name: broad_relatability_vs_insider_niche
conflict_axes.description: Broad scenes maximize reach but risk blandness; niche scenes maximize per-viewer intensity and shares but cap the ceiling.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: set the target point from the growth goal, then pick references and levers to fit it

conflict_axes.name: insider_reference_density_vs_first_contact_clarity
conflict_axes.description: Dense in-jokes raise resonance for insiders but can break instant comprehension for the broader viewer at scroll speed.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep references above a recognition threshold; gloss or cut those that fail the comprehension gate

conflict_axes.name: timing_window_urgency_vs_sensitivity_clearance
conflict_axes.description: A short topical window pressures fast publish, but the sensitivity gate needs time to clear topical ties safely.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: deadline creates urgency but the gate is a hard stop; drop unsafe topical ties

conflict_axes.name: format_familiarity_vs_freshness
conflict_axes.description: A familiar live format is an instant comprehension shortcut but an overused one signals lateness and lowers shareability.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: choose a format still live for the segment; refresh the turn within the familiar frame

conflict_axes.name: single_axis_legibility_vs_entity_richness
conflict_axes.description: One sharp contrast axis makes the incongruity legible but can flatten genuinely multidimensional entities.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: pick the one axis that best serves the turn; carry richness in secondary texture not the spine

conflict_axes.name: structure_economy_vs_template_fatigue
conflict_axes.description: Rigid setup/turn/punchline economy maximizes impact but an over-seen three-beat template reads as formulaic.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the economy; vary the surface so the structure is felt not seen

conflict_axes.name: shareability_optimization_vs_brand_trust
conflict_axes.description: Optimizing purely for shares can drift to outrage-bait that spreads but damages brand trust.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: prefer amusement/identity/surprise levers over anger; gate outrage-driven scenes

conflict_axes.name: narrative_richness_vs_attention_window
conflict_axes.description: A fuller micro-arc raises engagement but can bloat the scene past the platform's short attention window.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: imply the arc; cut any beat not serving the climax within the length norm

edge_cases.description: Two entities are forced together with no shared frame, producing a non-sequitur the audience cannot resolve.
edge_cases.trigger: entity bundle assembled without a relatedness check or a chosen contrast axis
edge_cases.mitigation: require a named relationship and a single contrast axis before assembly

edge_cases.description: The incongruity surprises but supplies no resolving rule, so the scene reads as random rather than funny.
edge_cases.trigger: a turn with no retrospective sense-making path for the target segment
edge_cases.mitigation: verify a resolving rule the segment can close; send back if confusion dominates

edge_cases.description: A violation lands as harmful (tragedy, ethnic/religious, punching-down) rather than benign and the scene causes offense.
edge_cases.trigger: violation aimed at a protected or vulnerable target with no benign distance
edge_cases.mitigation: relocate the violation off harmful targets and escalate ambiguous calls to compliance

edge_cases.description: A chosen meme format is dead or overused, signaling lateness and depressing shares despite a good joke.
edge_cases.trigger: format selected past its segment peak with no freshness check
edge_cases.mitigation: confirm the format is currently live for the segment before pouring the scene in

edge_cases.description: Dense insider references break first-contact comprehension for the broader target viewer.
edge_cases.trigger: reference density exceeds what the segment recognizes at scroll speed
edge_cases.mitigation: keep references above a recognition threshold; gloss or cut the rest

edge_cases.description: A topical tie attaches the scene to an unfolding tragedy or controversy and the scene blows up.
edge_cases.trigger: timing tie to a sensitive event bypasses the sensitivity gate under window pressure
edge_cases.mitigation: route every topical tie through the sensitivity gate; drop unsafe ties even mid-window

edge_cases.description: The attention window closes before publish, wasting time-sensitive work.
edge_cases.trigger: no freshness deadline set on a topical scene
edge_cases.mitigation: size the window and set a hard freshness deadline up front; abandon if missed

edge_cases.description: The punchline is not in terminal position, so the surprise leaks and impact drops.
edge_cases.trigger: comedic structure places the payload before the end or pads after it
edge_cases.mitigation: move the funniest element last and cut everything after the turn

edge_cases.description: The register fights the content, e.g. an edgy turn in an earnest brand voice, reading as tonally confused.
edge_cases.trigger: register chosen without agreement with the violation intensity
edge_cases.mitigation: align register with the violation intensity and hold it consistently

edge_cases.description: The scene is funny but optimized into outrage-bait that spreads while damaging brand trust.
edge_cases.trigger: shareability optimized on anger with no trust guardrail
edge_cases.mitigation: prefer amusement/identity/surprise levers; gate outrage-driven scenes

edge_cases.description: A harm emerges only from the combination of individually-fine parts and slips past idea-stage screening.
edge_cases.trigger: sensitivity checked only on the raw idea, not the assembled artifact
edge_cases.mitigation: re-screen the integrated artifact at the final gate, not just the concept

edge_cases.description: The scene is clear only to its author and a fresh viewer cannot decode the entities or turn at scroll speed.
edge_cases.trigger: comprehension assumed from the author's seat with no fresh-viewer test
edge_cases.mitigation: test first-contact comprehension on a fresh target-segment viewer with no caption

workflow.description: Pick 2-3 genuinely related entities and confirm a shared frame and named relationship.
workflow.gate: 2-3 related entities with an explicit shared frame

workflow.description: Name the target segment, inventory its shared schema and platform norms.
workflow.gate: segment named with a concrete reference schema

workflow.description: Choose the single contrast axis that orders all entities legibly.
workflow.gate: exactly one axis ordering all 2-3 entities

workflow.description: Build the setup, incongruity, and a resolution the segment can close.
workflow.gate: setup, incongruity, and a segment-closable resolution present

workflow.description: Set the violation intensity into the band that is felt yet stays benign.
workflow.gate: violation detectable and judged benign for the segment

workflow.description: Order setup/turn/punchline with the payload last; shape the micro-arc.
Choose a live meme format and map entities to its slots.
workflow.gate: format currently live; slots map to entities and turn

workflow.description: Integrate entities, format, axis, beats, and register into one coherent draft.
workflow.gate: single coherent unit with all entities placed

workflow.description: Test first-contact comprehension on a fresh segment viewer with no caption.
workflow.gate: entities and turn comprehended within the scroll window

workflow.description: Score resolution, benignity, and sample amusement; diagnose the weakest link.
workflow.gate: incongruity resolves and sample finds it amusing

workflow.description: Re-screen the assembled artifact for harm; require compliance sign-off for escalations.
workflow.gate: assembled scene clean; escalations signed off

workflow.description: Count share levers, estimate recognition, confirm window open, then package for publish.
workflow.gate: share levers and open window confirmed; gates passed

dominance_rules.rule: ENTITY_BUNDLE relatedness and a single ENTITY_CONTRAST_AXIS must be fixed before INCONGRUITY_RESOLUTION is engineered
dominance_rules.rationale: the incongruity is drawn along the contrast axis; building humor on an unrelated bundle yields a non-sequitur
dominance_rules.trigger: incongruity design begins on an unrelated bundle or with no axis
dominance_rules.action: block until a named relationship and one axis exist

dominance_rules.rule: SENSITIVITY_GATE is a hard stop that overrides HUMOR_QUALITY_SCORE and SHAREABILITY_FORECAST
dominance_rules.rationale: a funny, highly-shareable scene that fails the harm gate must not ship
dominance_rules.trigger: a scene passes humor and forecast but fails sensitivity
dominance_rules.action: block publish regardless of humor or forecast scores

dominance_rules.rule: BENIGN_VIOLATION must keep the violation benign before edge is maximized for shares
dominance_rules.rationale: violation that crosses into harm spreads damage, not just reach
dominance_rules.trigger: edge is pushed for shareability past the benign band
dominance_rules.action: relocate the violation off harmful targets or escalate

dominance_rules.rule: SENSITIVITY_AWARENESS must escalate any ambiguous harm call to compliance rather than deciding it in the writing seat
dominance_rules.rationale: a single writer should not absorb a legal/ethical adjudication
dominance_rules.trigger: an ambiguous harmful-framing case is resolved by the writer
dominance_rules.action: route the case to compliance and hold publish

dominance_rules.rule: CLARITY_READABILITY must pass before HUMOR_QUALITY_SCORE is trusted
dominance_rules.rationale: a scene that is not comprehended cannot be fairly judged funny
dominance_rules.trigger: humor scored on a scene that fails first-contact comprehension

dominance_rules.rule: TIMING_RELEVANCE topical ties must clear SENSITIVITY_GATE even under window pressure
dominance_rules.rationale: an unsafe topical tie causes outsized harm precisely because it is timely
dominance_rules.trigger: a topical tie is published to beat a closing window without the gate
dominance_rules.action: drop the tie or the scene; never bypass the gate

dominance_rules.rule: MEME_FORMAT_REUSE must confirm the format is currently live for the segment before SCENE_ASSEMBLY pours the scene in
dominance_rules.rationale: assembling around a dead format wastes layout work and signals lateness
dominance_rules.trigger: assembly proceeds on an unverified or stale format

dominance_rules.rule: RELATABILITY_VS_NICHE target point must be set from the growth goal before CULTURAL_REFERENCE density is chosen
dominance_rules.rationale: reference density should follow the reach-vs-depth decision, not drive it
dominance_rules.trigger: reference density chosen before the reach-vs-depth point
dominance_rules.action: fix the target point first, then choose references

dominance_rules.rule: SCENE_ASSEMBLY must reconcile format, beats, axis, and register before any evaluation gate runs
dominance_rules.rationale: gates judge the integrated artifact, not loose parts; evaluating fragments wastes review
dominance_rules.trigger: an evaluation gate runs on an un-integrated draft
dominance_rules.action: require a single coherent draft before gating

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not engineer the incongruity before the entity relationship and contrast axis are fixed; an axis change invalidates the whole joke
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rebuilding the humor core after a late axis or relationship change

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not push edge for shares before confirming the violation stays benign; harm found later forces a full rewrite or a takedown
anti_rework_rules.prevents: emergency rewrite or post-publish takedown after a harm complaint

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not assemble the scene around a meme format without confirming it is live; a dead format means redoing the layout
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-laying-out the scene after discovering the format is stale

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not load dense insider references before setting the reach-vs-depth point; over-niche references cap reach and need stripping
anti_rework_rules.prevents: stripping references and re-pacing after a reach-ceiling miss

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not run evaluation gates on un-integrated fragments; fragment fixes do not survive integration
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-reviewing the same scene after parts are finally integrated

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not screen sensitivity only on the raw idea; harms that emerge from combination force late, expensive rework
anti_rework_rules.prevents: killing a fully produced scene at the final gate over an emergent harm

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not commit to a register that fights the violation intensity; a tonal mismatch means re-voicing the whole scene
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-voicing the entire scene after a tonal-confusion review note

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not skip the freshness deadline on a topical scene; a missed window means the work is wasted and reworked as evergreen
anti_rework_rules.prevents: salvaging a missed-window scene into an evergreen format under pressure

iteration_protocol.trigger: a target-segment sample reports confusion rather than amusement
iteration_protocol.action: diagnose whether the resolution rule or the comprehension is at fault and revise INCONGRUITY_RESOLUTION or CLARITY_READABILITY

iteration_protocol.trigger: a harm complaint or near-miss is reported on a benign-violation call
iteration_protocol.action: relocate the violation off the harmful target and tighten the escalation trigger in SENSITIVITY_AWARENESS

iteration_protocol.trigger: a scene underperforms on shares despite passing humor and clarity
iteration_protocol.action: re-audit the share levers and reference recognition in SHAREABILITY_DRIVERS and SHAREABILITY_FORECAST

iteration_protocol.trigger: a chosen meme format proves dead or overused after assembly
iteration_protocol.action: re-select a live format in MEME_FORMAT_REUSE and re-pour the scene in SCENE_ASSEMBLY

iteration_protocol.trigger: a topical tie's attention window closes before publish
iteration_protocol.action: tighten window sizing and the freshness deadline in TIMING_RELEVANCE or abandon the topical angle

iteration_protocol.trigger: the audience misreads which contrast axis is in play
iteration_protocol.action: sharpen or re-select the axis in ENTITY_CONTRAST_AXIS and re-test comprehension

iteration_protocol.trigger: reviewers flag tonal confusion between register and content
iteration_protocol.action: realign the register with the violation intensity in TONE_REGISTER and re-assemble

iteration_protocol.trigger: a reach-ceiling miss shows the scene was too niche for the goal
iteration_protocol.action: reset the reach-vs-depth point in RELATABILITY_VS_NICHE and adjust reference density in CULTURAL_REFERENCE

priority_rationale: ENTITY_BUNDLE, AUDIENCE_FIT and the humor engine (INCONGRUITY_RESOLUTION/BENIGN_VIOLATION) are foundational; ENTITY_CONTRAST_AXIS, structure, format and beats feed SCENE_ASSEMBLY; CLARITY/HUMOR/SENSITIVITY/SHAREABILITY gates and the handoff close the method, with the sensitivity gate dominating as a hard stop.
